body.p: Support for this amendment is found within the filed specification at least at page 7, lines 16-23, and FIG. 3B (end of 370 when native sensor data 360B begins to be provided). Based on the amendment, the claims should be interpreted based on the other interpretation given by the Examiner on page 3 of the Office Action, or that the pseudo sensor data is entirely not being derived, because a response was received that there was an indication that the user equipment or sensor is providing native sensor data for the user. The Examiner is respectfully requested to withdraw the rejections based on Sections 102 and 103, because the prior art does not disclose or suggest the subject matter of the independent claims. MPEP 2143.03 ("All words in a claim must be considered in judging the patentability of that claim against the prior art.").

1. Independent claims 16, 27, 35: the prior art does not disclose or suggest wherein the pseudo sensor data is compatible with an application programming interface of the application, and the radio frequency based data is not compatible with the application programming interface of the application
Independent claims 16, 27, 35 have been amended to claim:

p.u: "wherein the pseudo sensor data is compatible with an application
interface of the application, and the radio fre
uency based data is not compatible with the
application programming interface of the application."

body.p: Support for this amendment is found within Applicant's filed specification at least at page 4, lines 9-14, and page 12, lines 16-17.
Gillian paragraph [0093] describes "a radar feature indicative of a characteristic of the target is extracted from the radar data."
Gillian paragraph [0096] describes "the augmented radar feature is provided to a sensor-based application."

The Examiner stated on page 20 of the Office Action that Gillian at the above-referenced excerpts ([0093], [0096]) describes the aspect of claim 31, or "wherein the pseudo sensor data is compatible with an application programming interface of the health and fitness tracker application, and the radio frequency based data is not compatible with the application programming interface of the health and fitness tracker application."

The Examiner stated on page 20 of the Office Action that the sensor based application takes the augmented radar feature; the sensor based application would not be able to create an augmented radar feature with raw radar data:

This is because Gillian does not describe that the sensor based application would not be able to process the raw radar data. At best, Gillian at paragraph [0063] describes generating a desired data format based on the raw data: "Once the raw data is generated, the signal

transformer 502 pre-processes the raw data to clean up the signals or generate versions of the signals in a desired frequency band or desired data format." However in this case, the reformatted radar data is radio frequency based data that may be compatible with the sensor based application (Gillian does not describe whether the reformatted data is compatible with the sensor-based application or not).

Gillian at paragraph [0075] actually describes the opposite of what is claimed by Applicant, indicating that the radar data is provided to the sensor based application. Gillian paragraph [0075] describes "The sensor fusion engine 110 provides or exposes the sensor data 506, radar data 508, or various combinations thereof to sensor-based applications 108 and the context manager 112."

In contrast, Applicant claims that the radio frequency based data is not compatible with an application programming interface of the application that enables tracking user activity, which is the reason for deriving the pseudo sensor data. This motivation is described within Applicant's specification at page 4, lines 11-14 ("However, this RF based data may not be readily processed by health and fitness tracker applications having application programming interfaces (APIs) accustomed to operating with, for example, sensor data, such as x-y-z accelerometer data or other types of sensor data, indicative of the user's activity") and page 12, lines 16-17 ("the application 390 may have an application programming interface configured to receive the pseudo sensor data"). This motivation is not disclosed or suggested by Gillian.

Accordingly, the prior art does not disclose or suggest wherein the pseudo sensor data is compatible with an application programming interface of the application, and the radio frequency based data is not compatible with the application programming interface of the application. Independent claims 16, 27, 35, on the other hand, claim "wherein the pseudo sensor data is compatible with an application programming interface of the application, and the radio frequency based data is not compatible with the application programming interface of the application." This is not disclosed or suggested by the prior art. Therefore, independent claims 16, 27, 35 are patentable and should be allowed.
2. Even if it was obvious to combine the references, they do not disclose or suggest all of the elements/features of the claims, as explained above

Applicant respectfully traverses the rationale to combine the references to support a rejection under Section 103. For example, because the prior art does not disclose or suggest wherein the pseudo sensor data is compatible with an application programming interface of the application, and the radio frequency based data is not compatible with the application programming interface of the application, one skilled in the art would not be motivated to combine the references to arrive at Applicant's claimed invention. Even if, for the sake of argument, it was obvious to combine the references, they do not disclose or suggest all of the elements/features of the claims, as explained above.
3. Dependent claims

Though the other dependent claims contain their own allowable subject matter, these claims should at least be allowable due to their dependence from allowable independent claims. However, to expedite prosecution at this time, no further comment will be made.

The Applicant respectfully requests the Examiner enter this amendment and pass the claims to issue. The undersigned representative welcomes the opportunity to resolve any matters that may remain, formal or otherwise, via teleconference at the Examiner's discretion.
